metadata.title: High-dimensional analysis of double descent for linear regression with random projections

nodes.name: (A1) Sub-Gaussian design
nodes.statement: $X = Z \Sigma^{1/2}$ with $Z \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ having sub-Gaussian i.i.d. components with mean zero and unit variance.
nodes.statement_clean: Design matrix factorizes as $Z \Sigma^{1/2}$ with sub-Gaussian iid entries.

nodes.name: (A2) High-dimensional aspect ratio
nodes.statement: Sample size $n$ and dimension $d$ go to infinity with $d/n \to \gamma > 0$.

nodes.name: (A3) Spectral measure converges
nodes.statement: The empirical spectral measure $\frac{1}{d} \sum_{i=1}^d \delta_{\sigma_i}$ of $\Sigma$ converges to a probability distribution $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}_+$ with compact support in $\mathbb{R}_+^*$; $\Sigma$ invertible and bounded in operator norm.

nodes.name: (A4) Signal spectral measure
nodes.statement: The measure $\sum_{i=1}^d (v_i^\top \theta_*)^2 \delta_{\sigma_i}$ converges to a measure $\nu$ with bounded mass; $\|\theta_*\|$ is bounded.

nodes.name: (A5) Sub-Gaussian random projection
nodes.statement: $S \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times m}$ has sub-Gaussian i.i.d. components with mean zero and unit variance.

nodes.name: (A6) Projection aspect ratio
nodes.statement: The number of projections $m$ tends to infinity with $m/n \to \delta > 0$.

nodes.name: Linear regression model
nodes.statement: $x_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are i.i.d. with covariance $\Sigma$; $y_i = x_i^\top \theta_* + \varepsilon_i$ with $\varepsilon_i$ independent of $x_i$, $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_i]=0$, $\mathrm{var}(\varepsilon_i)=\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Excess risk and bias-variance decomposition
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{R}(\hat\theta) = (\hat\theta - \theta_*)^\top \Sigma (\hat\theta - \theta_*)$, decomposed into bias term ($\sigma=0$) and variance term ($\theta_*=0$).

nodes.name: Empirical and kernel covariance matrices
nodes.statement: $\hat\Sigma = \frac{1}{n} X^\top X \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ is the empirical covariance; $XX^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is the kernel matrix.

nodes.name: Degrees of freedom $\mathrm{df}_1$ and $\mathrm{df}_2$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{df}_1(\kappa) = \mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma + \kappa I)^{-1}]$ and $\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa) = \mathrm{tr}[\Sigma^2 (\Sigma + \kappa I)^{-2}]$; classical effective dimensionalities.

nodes.name: Stieltjes transform $\hat\varphi$
nodes.statement: $\hat\varphi(z) = \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\left[\left(\frac{1}{n}XX^\top - z I\right)^{-1}\right] = \mathrm{tr}[(XX^\top - nz I)^{-1}]$ for $z \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}_+$.

nodes.name: Self-induced regularization $\kappa(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: $\kappa(\lambda) = 1/\varphi(-\lambda)$, the almost-sure limit of $1/\mathrm{tr}[(XX^\top + n\lambda I)^{-1}]$, satisfying the self-consistency equation $\kappa(\lambda) - \lambda \sim \kappa(\lambda) \cdot \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{df}_1(\kappa(\lambda))$.

nodes.name: Ridge regression estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat\theta = (X^\top X + n\lambda I)^{-1} X^\top y = X^\top (XX^\top + n\lambda I)^{-1} y$, the unique minimizer of $\frac{1}{n}\sum_i (y_i - x_i^\top \theta)^2 + \lambda \|\theta\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Minimum-norm least-squares estimator with random projections
nodes.statement: Given random projection $S \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times m}$, $\hat\eta$ is the minimum-norm minimizer of $\|y - XS\eta\|_2^2$, and $\hat\theta = S\hat\eta \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: Equivalent of $\mathrm{tr}[\hat\Sigma(\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}]$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{tr}[\hat\Sigma(\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}] \sim \mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma + \kappa(\lambda) I)^{-1}]$ for any $\lambda > 0$, where $\kappa : \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}_+$ is increasing.

nodes.name: Self-consistent Stieltjes equation
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{\varphi(z)} + z = \gamma \int_0^{+\infty} \frac{\sigma\, d\mu(\sigma)}{1 + \sigma \varphi(z)}$ for $z \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}_+$.

nodes.name: Closed-form $\kappa(\lambda)$ for isotropic $\Sigma$
nodes.statement: $\kappa(\lambda) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\lambda - \sigma(1-\gamma) + \sqrt{(\sigma(1-\gamma) - \lambda)^2 + 4\lambda\sigma}\right)$ when $\Sigma = \sigma I$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic equivalents for spectral functions of $\hat\Sigma$
nodes.statement: Under (A1)-(A3), $\mathrm{tr}[A\hat\Sigma(\hat\Sigma - z I)^{-1}] \sim \mathrm{tr}[A\Sigma(\Sigma + 1/\varphi(z) I)^{-1}]$, with an analogous quadratic equivalent involving a $1/(n - \mathrm{df}_2(1/\varphi(z)))$ correction.
assumptions: $\sum_i v_i^\top A v_i \delta_{\sigma_i} \to \nu_A$ and analogous for $B$ with bounded total variation
conclusions: Quadratic equivalent with explicit $\square = 1/(n - \mathrm{df}_2(1/\varphi(z)))$ correction term

nodes.name: Asymptotic equivalents for kernel-form spectral functions
nodes.statement: Under (A1)-(A3), $\mathrm{tr}[A Z^\top (Z\Sigma Z^\top - nz I)^{-1} Z] \sim \mathrm{tr}[A(\Sigma + 1/\varphi(z) I)^{-1}]$, with the quadratic version replacing $\Sigma^{1/2} A \Sigma^{1/2}$ by $A$.
assumptions: Limiting measures $\nu_A, \nu_B$ have bounded total variation
conclusions: $\mathrm{tr}[A Z^\top(Z\Sigma Z^\top - nz I)^{-1} Z] \sim \mathrm{tr}[A(\Sigma + 1/\varphi(z) I)^{-1}]$

nodes.name: Random-design ridge regression bias and variance
nodes.statement: Under (A1)-(A4), the variance of ridge regression is $\sim \frac{\sigma^2}{n}\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda)) / (1 - \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda)))$ and the bias is $\sim \kappa(\lambda)^2 \theta_*^\top \Sigma(\Sigma + \kappa(\lambda) I)^{-2} \theta_* / (1 - \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda)))$.
assumptions: Ridge regression estimator $\hat\theta = (X^\top X + n\lambda I)^{-1} X^\top y$

nodes.name: Random projections: asymptotic bias and variance (double descent)
nodes.statement: Under (A1)-(A6), the minimum-norm random-projection estimator obeys: under-parameterized ($m<n$) variance $\sim \sigma^2 m/(n-m)$ and bias $\sim \kappa_m \theta_*^\top \Sigma(\Sigma + \kappa_m I)^{-1}\theta_* / (1 - m/n)$ with $\mathrm{df}_1(\kappa_m) \sim m$; over-parameterized ($m>n$) variance and bias have additional $\sigma^2 n/(m-n)$ and $\kappa_n \theta_*^\top \Sigma(\Sigma+\kappa_n I)^{-1}\theta_* \cdot n/(m-n)$ terms with $\mathrm{df}_1(\kappa_n) \sim n$.
assumptions: Minimum-norm least-squares estimator with random projections $\hat\theta = S\hat\eta$

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur distribution (cited)
nodes.statement: When $\Sigma = \sigma I$, inversion of the Stieltjes transform $\varphi(z)$ recovers the Marchenko-Pastur distribution as the limiting spectral distribution of $\frac{1}{n}XX^\top$.

nodes.name: Hanson-Wright inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For sub-Gaussian iid vector $z_i$ and matrix $N$: $\mathbb{P}[|z_i^\top N z_i - \mathrm{tr}(N)| \leq c(t\|N\|_{\mathrm{op}} + \sqrt{t}\|N\|_F)] \geq 1 - 2e^{-t}$.

nodes.name: Proof of random-design ridge regression bias-variance
nodes.statement: Apply trace equivalents from Prop. 1 with $A=I, B=\Sigma, z=-\lambda$, then simplify variance via $\kappa\,\mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma+\kappa I)^{-2}] = \mathrm{df}_1(\kappa) - \mathrm{df}_2(\kappa)$; for bias apply equivalent with $A=\Sigma, B=\theta_*\theta_*^\top$.

nodes.name: Proof of random-projections double descent
nodes.statement: Use $\ell_2$-regularized estimator with $\lambda \to 0$. Treat under- and over-parameterized regimes separately, expanding first w.r.t. $X$ then $S$ (under) and vice versa (over), using kernel-form Prop. 2.

nodes.name: Proof of self-consistent Stieltjes equation
nodes.statement: Three-step argument following Silverstein 1995: rewrite via matrix inversion lemma, isolate negligible $\Delta$ term using Hanson-Wright, then combine identities to derive self-consistent equation for $\varphi(z)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Propositions 1 and 2 (spectral equivalents)
nodes.statement: Differentiate self-consistent equation to bound $\varphi/\varphi'$, derive equivalent for $\mathrm{tr}[(\hat\Sigma - zI)^{-2}]$, then handle quadratic forms via diagonal-vs-off-diagonal decomposition with $\square$ correction term.

nodes.name: Variance trace identity
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}_\varepsilon[\mathcal{R}^{(\mathrm{var})}(\hat\theta)] = \frac{\sigma^2}{n}\mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-2}\hat\Sigma]$, expanded as a difference of $\mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\hat\Sigma+\lambda I)^{-1}]$ and $\lambda \mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-2}]$.

nodes.name: Apply spectral equivalents to variance
nodes.statement: Apply equations (trA2) and (trAB2) with $A=I$, $B=\Sigma$, $z=-\lambda$ to obtain expressions in terms of $\Sigma$, $\kappa(\lambda)$, $\mathrm{df}_1$, $\mathrm{df}_2$.

nodes.name: Simplify using $\mathrm{df}_1, \mathrm{df}_2$ identity
nodes.statement: Use $\kappa\, \mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma+\kappa I)^{-2}] = \mathrm{df}_1(\kappa) - \mathrm{df}_2(\kappa)$ and the self-consistency relation to collapse to $\sigma^2 \mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda))/(n - \mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda)))$.

nodes.name: Bias decomposition
nodes.statement: Write $\mathcal{R}^{(\mathrm{bias})}(\hat\theta) = \lambda^2 \theta_*^\top (\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}\Sigma(\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}\theta_*$.

nodes.name: Apply (trAB2) for bias
nodes.statement: Apply equation (trAB2) with $A=\Sigma$, $B=\theta_*\theta_*^\top$ (valid by (A4)) to get the bias equivalent with the $1/(n-\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda)))$ correction.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Collect terms to obtain $\mathcal{R}^{(\mathrm{bias})}(\hat\theta) \sim \kappa(\lambda)^2 \theta_*^\top \Sigma(\Sigma+\kappa(\lambda) I)^{-2}\theta_* \cdot (1 + \mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda))/(n - \mathrm{df}_2(\kappa(\lambda))))$.

nodes.name: Under-parameterized: variance via $X$-expansion
nodes.statement: For $S$ fixed, under-parameterized regime gives $\mathcal{R}^{(\mathrm{var})}(\hat\theta) \sim \frac{\sigma^2}{n-m}\mathrm{tr}(S^\top \Sigma S(S^\top \Sigma S)^{-1}) = \sigma^2 m/(n-m)$, independent of $S$.

nodes.name: Under-parameterized: bias via $C = TT^\top$
nodes.statement: Set $T = \Sigma^{1/2}S$, $C = TT^\top$. Apply Prop. 2 with covariance $C$ and degrees-of-freedom $\widetilde{\kappa}$ to expand the bias in terms of $A=C\Sigma^{1/2}\theta_*\theta_*^\top \Sigma^{1/2}$ and $B=C^2$.

nodes.name: Under-parameterized: take $\lambda \to 0$
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda \to 0$ so $\widetilde\kappa \to 0$ and $C(C+\widetilde\kappa I)^{-1} \to \Sigma^{1/2}S(S^\top \Sigma S)^{-1}S^\top \Sigma^{1/2}$, yielding equation (biasA): $\theta_*^\top(\Sigma - \Sigma S(S^\top \Sigma S)^{-1}S^\top \Sigma)\theta_* (1 + m/(n-m))$.

nodes.name: Under-parameterized: full expansion w.r.t. $S$
nodes.statement: Apply Prop. 2 again with $Z = S^\top$, covariance $\Sigma$, and $\kappa_m$ defined by $\mathrm{df}_1(\kappa_m) = m$ to get $\Sigma - \Sigma S(S^\top \Sigma S)^{-1}S^\top \Sigma \sim \Sigma - \Sigma^{1/2}(\Sigma + \kappa_m I)^{-1}\Sigma^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Over-parameterized: expansion w.r.t. $S$
nodes.statement: Use Prop. 2 with covariance $\hat\Sigma$ to expand the variance and bias traces, then take $\lambda \to 0$ using identities for $\hat\Sigma(\hat\Sigma + \widetilde\kappa I)^{-2}$ to derive equations (varB) and (biasC).

nodes.name: Over-parameterized: full expansion via $\kappa_n$
nodes.statement: Apply Prop. 2 once more with $\kappa_n$ such that $\mathrm{df}_1(\kappa_n) = n$, combining (varB) and (biasC) to obtain the over-parameterized variance and bias equivalents involving $\sigma^2 n/(m-n)$.

nodes.name: First step: matrix inversion lemma identity
nodes.statement: Use the matrix inversion lemma to rewrite $\mathrm{tr}[X^\top X(X^\top X - nzI)^{-1}]$ as $n - \sum_i 1/(1 + x_i^\top (\hat\Sigma_{-i} - zI)^{-1} x_i)$, leading to identity $-z\hat\varphi(z) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i 1/(\cdots)$.

nodes.name: Second step: isolate negligible $\Delta$
nodes.statement: Define $\Delta$ such that $(\hat\Sigma - zI)^{-1} = (-z\hat\varphi(z)\Sigma - zI)^{-1}(I - \Delta)$. Show $\Delta$ is asymptotically negligible by Hanson-Wright concentration and i.i.d. assumption on $z_i$.

nodes.name: Third step: combine identities
nodes.statement: Combine (proofB) and (proofC) following Silverstein to derive $\hat\varphi(z) \to \varphi(z)$ with the self-consistent equation $\varphi(z) + 1/z = \frac{1}{nz}\mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma + 1/\varphi(z) I)^{-1}]$.

nodes.name: Differentiate self-consistent equation
nodes.statement: Differentiate the self-consistent equation w.r.t. $z$ to obtain $\varphi/\varphi' = \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma + 1/\varphi(z) I)^{-2}] / \varphi(z)^2 - z$.

nodes.name: Equivalent for $\mathrm{tr}[(\hat\Sigma - zI)^{-2}]$
nodes.statement: Derive $\mathrm{tr}[\hat\Sigma(\hat\Sigma - zI)^{-2}] \sim n\,\mathrm{tr}[\Sigma(\Sigma + 1/\varphi(z) I)^{-2}] / (n - \mathrm{df}_2(1/\varphi(z)))$ to access the $\square$ correction.

nodes.name: Linear trace equivalent (eq. trA1/trA2)
nodes.statement: Show $\mathrm{tr}[A(\hat\Sigma - zI)^{-1}] \sim \mathrm{tr}[A(-z\hat\varphi(z)\Sigma - zI)^{-1}]$ via the $\Delta$-negligibility argument from Appendix A.1.

nodes.name: Quadratic trace equivalent (eq. trAB1/trAB2)
nodes.statement: Expand $(\hat\Sigma - zI)^{-1}$ via $(I - \Delta)$, identify cross-term involving $\sum_i \mathrm{tr}[\cdots(x_ix_i^\top - \Sigma)\cdots(x_ix_i^\top-\Sigma)\cdots]$, and reduce to $\mathrm{tr}(M)\mathrm{tr}(N)$ scaled by $\square$ via Hanson-Wright.

nodes.name: Compute $\square$ via $A=B=I$ specialization
nodes.statement: Specialize to $A=B=I$ to identify $\square = z^2\varphi(z)^2 / (n - \mathrm{df}_2(1/\varphi(z)))$, completing the quadratic equivalent.

nodes.name: Isotropic covariance and Marchenko-Pastur
nodes.statement: When $\Sigma = \sigma I$, the closed-form $\kappa(\lambda)$ has three regimes: $\gamma<1$ ($\kappa(0)=0$, $\kappa'(0) = 1/(1-\gamma)$); $\gamma>1$ ($\kappa(0) = (\gamma-1)\sigma > 0$); $\gamma=1$ ($\kappa \sim \sqrt{\lambda}$).

nodes.name: Power-law eigenvalues (kernel methods)
nodes.statement: For eigenvalues $\lambda_k = \tau/k^\alpha$ with $\alpha>1$ rescaled by $d^\alpha$, degrees of freedom satisfy $\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa d^\alpha) \sim (\tau/\kappa)^{1/\alpha}\int_0^\infty dv/(1+v^\alpha)$, giving the classical $\kappa^{-1/\alpha}$ explosion.

nodes.name: Two-Dirac spectral measure simulations
nodes.statement: Spectral measure $\mu = \pi_1\delta_{\sigma_1} + \pi_2\delta_{\sigma_2}$ with $\nu = \mu$, $\gamma = d/n = 2$. Empirical bias and variance match asymptotic equivalents as $n$ grows; conjectured rate $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ almost surely, $O(1/n)$ in expectation.

nodes.name: Double descent with $1/k$ eigenvalues
nodes.statement: $\Sigma$ of size $d=400$, $n=200$, eigenvalues $\propto 1/k$, normalized so $\tr\Sigma = 1$. With $\theta_*$ Gaussian and $\theta_*^\top \Sigma\theta_*=1$, plotted bias and variance show full double descent and U-shape on bias under-parameterized.

nodes.name: Isotropic eigenvalues: no U-shape
nodes.statement: Same setup as Ex 4 but with uniform (isotropic) eigenvalues; the bias does NOT exhibit a U-shape under-parameterized, so the bias+variance has no U-shape.

nodes.name: Self-induced regularization is implicit
nodes.statement: $\kappa(\lambda) \geq \lambda$ always; the gap is the additional regularization induced by random design, beyond the explicit $\lambda$ used in ridge.

nodes.name: Catastrophic vs benign over-fitting
nodes.statement: When $\mathrm{df}_2(\kappa) \ll \mathrm{df}_1(\kappa) = n$ (unbalanced regime), the variance can vanish as $n \to \infty$; otherwise (equivalent regime) variance is proportional to $\sigma^2$ and noise prevents good performance.

nodes.name: Random projections vs sketching
nodes.statement: Random projections multiply $X$ on the right ($XS$); sketching multiplies $y, X$ on the left ($Ty, TX$). They differ structurally; this paper analyzes the right-multiplication case.

nodes.name: Optimal $m$ in the over-parameterized regime
nodes.statement: Once $m > n$, the bias and variance are decreasing in $m$, so it is always best to take $m$ as large as possible. The $m=\infty$ limit is achievable directly via $\hat\theta = X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}y$ without solving an $m$-dimensional problem.

nodes.name: Ridge regression objective
nodes.statement: $\hat\theta = \arg\min_\theta \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - x_i^\top\theta)^2 + \lambda\|\theta\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Minimum-norm least squares with random projections
nodes.statement: $\hat\eta = \arg\min_{\eta : \|y - XS\eta\|_2^2 \text{ minimal}} \|\eta\|_2$, with $\hat\theta = S\hat\eta$.
